newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Peso-dollar parity to stay-Argentina's Fernandez.
newsitem.headline: Peso-dollar parity to stay-Argentina's Fernandez.

text.p: Argentina's Economy Minister Roque Fernandez Wednesday dismissed opposition calls for an end to the six-year-old peso-dollar parity.
"No problem in Argentina will be solved" by putting an end to the one-peso-one-dollar system enshrined in the Convertibility law, he told a TV interviewer.

He was reacting to recent remarks by former Argentine president and opposition Radical Party leader Raul Alfonsin, who said that, although not immediately, the country should start thinking of ways out of convertibility.
Fernandez said Argentina will only change the peso-dollar parity once a common currency is adopted by the Mercosur customs union with Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
A common currency is not a Mercosur priority and may be several years down the road.

Fernandez also called "a step forward" an agreement in principle hammered out Friday between the CGT main union federation and the government on labor reforms. The government considers those reforms crucial to bring unemployment down from its near-record level of 17.3 percent.
But businessmen have expressed objections to the deal and earlier Wednesday President Carlos Menem complained that "months and months have been lost" in pursuit of consensus.
He also warned Congress that unless it supported his labor reforms plans he might attempt again to implement them by presidential decree.
